phrases.text: So welcome back again. Time for one more problem. Now, in this problem, a hiker travels a total distance of forty kilometer in five hours. He covers some part on foot at five kilometers per hour.
He covers the remaining part on a bicycle at fifteen kilometers per hour.
The question is asking us to find the distance traveled on foot.
Let us take the distance traveled on foot as X kilometer.
The total distance is forty kilometer.
So after walking X kilometer,
the distance left for the bicycle is forty minus X kilometer.
Now, both distances are clear. The walking distance is X and the cycling distance is forty minus X.
Next,
let us find the time taken for each part.
We know that time is equal to distance divided by speed. For the walking part, the distance is X and the speed is five,
so the walking time is X divided by five hours.
For the cycling part,
the distance is forty minus
X
and the speed is fifteen, so the cycling time is forty minus x divided by fifteen hours. The hiker spends some time walking and the remaining time cycling.
When we add these two times,
we must get the total journey time of
five hours.
So x divided by five
plus forty minus
x divided by fifteen is equal to five.
Now, let us solve this equation.
The LCM of five and fifteen is fifteen.
Multiplying the complete equation by fifteen,
we get three x
plus forty minus x equal to seventy-five.
Combining the x terms,
we get two x plus forty equal to seventy-five.
Now, subtracting forty from both sides,
we get two x equal to thirty-five.
Dividing both sides by two,
we get x equal to seventeen point five.
Remember, x represents the distance traveled on foot.
Hence,
the hiker traveled
seventeen point five kilometers on foot.
So the final answer will be option B, seventeen point five kilometers.
